purpose: Requirements for the ADR writer, an isolated agent that judges, repairs and records ADRs apart from the design flow, returning a create, reject or insufficient verdict.
summary: Overview: ADR writer separates ADR judgment and writing from the design context
Terms: ADR file, decision section, request, type (approval record, judgment record, update), verdict
FNC-001 and FNC-002: request intake with types, and rejection criteria for judgment records
FNC-003 and FNC-004: fixing malformed content before writing; returning what is missing instead of inventing facts
FNC-005: approval records are never rejected, only checked for completeness of required quote and reason
FNC-006: updating a rejected decision by rewriting the same section, moving the old idea into alternatives
FNC-007: verdict return values (create, reject, insufficient) and failure visibility
FNC-008 and FNC-009: one ADR file per feature under adr/ with numbered naming, write scope limited to ADR files
FNC-010 to FNC-012: single entry point, start-design not holding ADR norms, single source for ADR norms
NFR: isolated context and failure visibility
tasks: Designing or revising the ADR writer agent or skill
Writing or updating an ADR file
Requesting an approval record when a design departs from requirements
Deciding whether a decision deserves an ADR
Updating or retracting an existing ADR decision
Modifying start-design to delegate ADR work
Reviewing ADR writer behavior against requirements
Choosing ADR output location and file naming
